operator_io_quirks: Two tables are quoted mixed-case in DDL: "movie_keywords", "movie_company" — must be double-quoted in generated SQL; column lookup case-insensitive.
movie_keywords/movie_company FKs use inline `references movie` / `references keyword` with NULL parent column -> parent column = same name as child (movie_id, keyword_id, company_id).
movie_keywords.keyword_id references keyword (parent col NULL -> keyword_id); movie_company.company_id references production_company (parent col NULL -> company_id).

movie.release_date declared DATE but storage class is text, format %Y-%m-%d (e.g. 1995-12-09); ts_fuzzer dispatch = Date|Number(int elements) — first element '1995-12-09' does not parse as int so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d.
movie.popularity / vote_average declared REAL, storage real, values like 22.87623 — Number fuzzer with scale from no args (default).
movie.budget/revenue INTEGER with large values (up to ~9e8) — Number fuzzer int scale default; perturb +-1/+-2 tiny relative to magnitude.
language.language_name has non-ASCII text (u65e5u672cu8a9e) and 63 distinct vs 88 rows — duplicates exist; String fuzzer will not reproduce unicode.
movie.homepage has empty-string values and long URLs; String fuzzer length range from elements (min len 0).
movie.title 4625 distinct vs 4627 rows — duplicate titles; person_name 103147 vs 104838; company_name 5017 vs 5047 — non-unique text columns.

movie_genres, movie_languages, movie_crew, movie_cast, production_country, movie_keywords, movie_company have NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op; only unique-column dedup applies (none declared unique).
All FK parent tables exist (parent_exists true everywhere); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite PKs.
Largest tables: movie_crew 129581, person 104838, movie_cast 59083 — under 300000 cap, full read OK; no rowid sampling needed.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on movie.release_date: template %Y-%m-%d, range from parsed elements (~1970..2015), fresh dates uniform in that range; p=0.2 means element returned w.p. 0.2.
Number fuzzer on all *_id INTEGER PKs: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with default scale, so fresh PKs are huge ints far from original small ids (1..N) — implausible but valid.

String fuzzer on title/person_name/company_name/character_name: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length in [min,max] of elements, plus contaminate suffix/prefix — implausible names, drives FN on LIKE/equality predicates.
String fuzzer on country_iso_code (2-char codes) and language_code: length range [2,2] so fresh strings are 2 chars — plausible-ish but random letters, misses real ISO codes.
String fuzzer on movie_status (3 distinct: Released/Rumored/Post Production) and gender (3 distinct): fresh random strings break equality predicates -> FN.

Number fuzzer on movie.budget/revenue/runtime/vote_count: fresh draws uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale default 0 -> [-1,1]? actually scale from type args absent -> default) — likely tiny ints, misses large real values -> FN on range predicates.
Number fuzzer on movie.popularity/vote_average REAL: fresh floats uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale], perturb +-0.01/0.02 — misses real 0..150 range -> FN.

FK columns (movie_genres.movie_id etc.) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement — ties/duplicates preserved, so join cardinalities plausible; but parent PK filtering drops rows so child may reference fewer parents.
No PK on junction tables -> no dedup -> duplicate (movie_id,genre_id) pairs possible, unlike original which has 12160 rows over 4775 movies — FP risk on COUNT(DISTINCT) vs COUNT.

movie_genres.genre_id distinct 20 but samples show 878 (out of range) — original has FK violations? genre_id 878 not in genre(20 rows) — TS FK fill will only use valid genre ids, so original's dangling genre_id 878 not reproduced.
String fuzzer on overview/tagline/homepage: long text replaced by short random strings -> FN on length/LIKE predicates; empty homepage reproduced only via element sampling.
Number fuzzer on cast_order (0..212): fresh ints in full range, misses small ordering values -> FN on ORDER BY / cast_order < k predicates.
